recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-12637 unless a future work-group decision reopens Timing semantics for event resources.
issue_request: FHIR-12637 was a Published/Persuasive MnM change request for DSTU2 asking to remove the Timing datatype sentence that said Timing schedules were not used for recording when things happened, only when expected or requested.
initial_application: Historical git-svn commit ed9e3b435c3f18ca0557747fbeb01b18b05619b1, referencing #12637 and svn revision 11269, removed the prohibitive sentence from source/datatypes.html and updated source/datatypes/timing.xml to allow planned, expected, requested, and past regular-activity timing schedules.
additional_context: Timing is active in source/fhir.ini and marked normative. The current source/datatypes.html Timing introduction says Timing may represent summaries of past or ongoing events. Later Published/Persuasive FHIR-13231, already audited on the combined branch, refined the same Timing event-use wording rather than reversing FHIR-12637. Zulip discussion around GF#12637 supports the need for broader wording, and Confluence searches found no conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because no source correction is needed in the current core FHIR checkout.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive Timing issue supplied the current broader introduction that explicitly allows summaries of past or ongoing events; it already has its own no-change audit on the combined branch.
